problem: The entropy equations are written for one mole, but the units given for the heat capacities do not match: CV is called J/K and CP is called J/K, while R is J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ and the equation dS = CV dT/T + R dV/V only works when S, CV and V are all per mole. The same mix-up carries into the worked example, where V is in m³ mol⁻¹.
fix: State that these forms are per mole: use molar heat capacities CV and CP in J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, molar entropy in J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, molar volume in m³ mol⁻¹, and note that the total-property forms are dS = CV dT/T + nR dV/V. Keep the separate statement that dU = CV dT uses the total CV in J/K when U is total.

problem: The answer ties the sign of S to the phase being 'stable'. Entropy is positive for any condensed or gaseous phase at ordinary temperature (third law reference), so stability is not the reason; a student may wrongly conclude an unstable phase has negative entropy or a positive slope.
fix: Say: (∂G/∂T)P = −S, and S > 0 for every phase at T above absolute zero, so G always falls as T rises at fixed pressure; stability is a separate point about the curvature, (∂²G/∂T²)P = −CP/T < 0.
